title: Unbounded in-memory dedup set leaks memory until the worker OOM-loops
source_note: Failure pattern (an unbounded in-memory collection grows with traffic until the process hits its memory limit and is OOM-killed on a repeating sawtooth, with GC pressure degrading throughput on the way up) is a standard resource-exhaustion class covered in the Google SRE Book. All services, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: notification-worker has been restarting repeatedly since around 05:00 UTC and the notification queue is falling behind. No deploys today; the last one was 3 days ago. Latency on the rest of the platform is normal.

signal_lines.msg: heap usage 78% and climbing steadily; does not track queue depth
heap 82%; GC pause time 400ms/min; processing lag growing
OOMKilled; restart #4; in-memory dedup set holds 14M entries and never evicts
operator added a size bound and TTL to the dedup set; heap stable

ground_truth.root_cause: notification-worker has a memory leak: an in-memory de-duplication set that is never bounded or evicted (observed holding 14M entries). As notification volume grew, the set's footprint climbed until the container hit its memory limit and was OOM-killed, restarting on a sawtooth. During each growth phase, GC pressure slowed processing and the work queue backed up. The leak predates today - the last deploy was 3 days ago - and only became visible now as volume crossed the threshold. Recovery required bounding the set with a size cap and TTL.
evidence_path: notification-worker heap climbs steadily from ~45%, independent of queue depth - a leak signature, not load
repeated OOMKilled restarts on a sawtooth (restart #1 ... #4)
the dedup set is observed holding 14M entries and never evicting
queue_lag grows during each heap-growth phase from GC pressure
no deploy today; the last deploy was 3 days ago
heap stabilises after a size bound and TTL are added to the set
ground_truth.fix: Bound the dedup set with a max size and TTL (done). Add a heap-growth-rate alert, audit other unbounded in-memory collections, and set the container memory limit from the real bounded working set.
